recommendation: Do not adopt augmentation now. Keep the official benchmark and the data-preparation pipeline free of synthetic data. Revisit only as a labelled, train-only sensitivity experiment after a Model 1 baseline exists, limited to masking and jitter on live non-constant entries.

methods.method: Gaussian jitter on live, non-constant entries
methods.advantage: cheap; mild regulariser for the 130-d numeric vectors
methods.risk: 80% of entries are exact zeros that carry meaning (series mean / absent block); adding noise to them invents signal. Incident deviations are brief spikes, so noise comparable to them can erase or fake a fault signature.
methods.verdict: possible later, train-only, never on zero/absent entries

methods.risk: features are one-minute aggregates with lag-1 autocorrelation median 0.64; warping changes the onset timing that defines the injection response, and windows crossing a split boundary would leak.
blends different fault classes or an incident with normal minutes into states that never occurred; labels become ill-defined (no incident durations exist).
the rarest class has 4 training cases; synthetic incidents would be fabricated ground truth and are prohibited in the benchmark.

methods.advantage: matches the missing-modality robustness goal and uses the real data unchanged
methods.risk: must keep structural absence separate from simulated absence (indicators); ARMOR already applies it in its own pretraining.
methods.verdict: already part of ARMOR; evaluate in Model 1 only with indicators

methods.risk: temporal leakage if it draws on samples after the training boundary.

leakage_rules_if_revisited: fit and draw only from the training period of an approved split
